ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle A=50^\circ$, and the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, $DE$, intersects $AC$ and $AB$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. What is the degree measure of $\angle CBD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=50^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=(180^\circ-50^\circ)÷2=65^\circ$ \\
Since $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ \\
$\therefore$ $DA=DB$ \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABD=\angle A=50^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBD=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=65^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{15^\circ}$

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as triangle ABC with A at the top, B lower left, C lower right; D lies on side AC, E lies on side AB, and segment DE crosses AB perpendicularly at E, with ray BD drawn inside angle ABC. From the text, use AB=AC and ∠A=50°. Therefore triangle ABC is isosceles, so ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°−50°)/2=65°. Since DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB and D is on DE, D is equidistant from A and B, so DA=DB. Because D is on AC, ∠DAB=∠CAB=50°. Thus triangle ABD is isosceles with DA=DB, giving ∠ABD=50°. Finally, since BD lies inside ∠ABC in the figure, ∠CBD=∠ABC−∠ABD=65°−50°=15°.

$\therefore$ $\angle CBD=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=65^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{15^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle A=50^\circ$, and the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, $DE$, intersects $AC$ and $AB$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. What is the degree measure of $\angle CBD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=50^\circ$ \\ $\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=(180^\circ-50^\circ)\div 2=65^\circ$ \\ Since $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ \\ $\therefore$ $DA=DB$ \\ $\therefore$ $\angle ABD=\angle A=50^\circ$ \\ $\therefore$ $\angle CBD=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=65^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{15^\circ}$

Image description: In the figure, the vertex A of triangle ABC is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right; D is located on side AC, and E is located on side AB; segment DE is perpendicular to AB at point E, indicating that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB; segment BD connects from B to D and is located inside angle ABC.
Reasoning: It is known that AB=AC and ∠A=50°, so △ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°−50°)/2=65°. Because DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, and D is on DE, the distances from D to A and B are equal, that is, DA=DB. Also because D is on AC, ∠DAB=∠CAB=50°. In △ABD, DA=DB, therefore the base angles ∠ABD=∠DAB=50°. It can be seen from the figure that BD is inside ∠ABC, so ∠CBD=∠ABC−∠ABD=65°−50°=15°.
